LUMO's Gospel of Luke in Oluluyia — a word-for-word film of Luke's Gospel with Oluluyia narration over cinematic footage. Presented as 24 chapters. Oluluyia is spoken mainly in Kenya by around 3,312,200 people.

Luke 1

Two Births Foretold

Luke 1

Luke 1

Two Births Foretold

The angel Gabriel announces the coming births of John the Baptist to Zechariah and of Jesus to the virgin Mary. Mary sings praise to God, and John is born to Elizabeth in her old age.

Luke 2

The Birth of Jesus

Luke 2

Luke 2

The Birth of Jesus

Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger, and angels announce the news to shepherds. He is presented in the temple, and at twelve years old amazes the teachers in his Father's house.

Luke 3

The Ministry of John the Baptist

Luke 3

Luke 3

The Ministry of John the Baptist

John preaches a baptism of repentance at the Jordan and points to one greater who is coming. Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends like a dove, and his family line is traced back to Adam.

Luke 4

Temptation and Rejection at Nazareth

Luke 4

Luke 4

Temptation and Rejection at Nazareth

Jesus fasts forty days in the wilderness and overcomes the devil's temptations with Scripture. In the Nazareth synagogue he announces that Isaiah's promise is fulfilled, and his own town drives him out.

Luke 5

Calling the First Disciples

Luke 5

Luke 5

Calling the First Disciples

After a miraculous catch of fish, Peter, James, and John leave their boats to follow Jesus. Jesus cleanses a leper, forgives and heals a paralyzed man, and calls Levi the tax collector.

Luke 6

Lord of the Sabbath

Luke 6

Luke 6

Lord of the Sabbath

Jesus declares the Son of Man Lord of the Sabbath and chooses twelve apostles. On a level place he blesses the poor, commands love for enemies, and tells of two builders — one on rock, one on sand.

Luke 7

The Centurion's Faith

Luke 7

Luke 7

The Centurion's Faith

Jesus marvels at a Roman centurion's faith and raises a widow's only son at Nain. He answers John the Baptist's question from prison, and a sinful woman washes his feet with her tears.

Luke 8

The Parable of the Sower

Luke 8

Luke 8

The Parable of the Sower

Jesus tells the parable of the sower and calms a storm with a word. He frees a man possessed by a legion of demons, heals a bleeding woman, and raises Jairus's daughter.

Luke 9

Feeding the Five Thousand

Luke 9

Luke 9

Feeding the Five Thousand

Jesus sends out the Twelve, feeds five thousand, and Peter confesses him as God's Messiah. On the mountain Jesus is transfigured in glory, then sets his face toward Jerusalem.

Luke 10

The Good Samaritan

Luke 10

Luke 10

The Good Samaritan

Jesus sends out seventy-two messengers ahead of him and rejoices in the Father's revelation to little children. He answers 'Who is my neighbor?' with the parable of the good Samaritan, and Mary chooses the better part at his feet.

Luke 11

Teaching on Prayer

Luke 11

Luke 11

Teaching on Prayer

Jesus teaches his disciples to pray, 'Father, hallowed be your name.' He casts out demons by the finger of God, and pronounces woes on Pharisees who clean the outside of the cup.

Luke 12

Do Not Be Afraid, Little Flock

Luke 12

Luke 12

Do Not Be Afraid, Little Flock

Jesus warns against hypocrisy and greed, telling of a rich fool whose life ends the night his barns are full. He calls his followers to trust the Father who feeds the ravens, and to be ready for the Son of Man's coming.

Luke 13

The Narrow Door

Luke 13

Luke 13

The Narrow Door

Jesus calls all to repent, heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath, and likens the kingdom to a mustard seed. He urges entry through the narrow door and weeps over Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets.

Luke 14

The Great Banquet

Luke 14

Luke 14

The Great Banquet

At a Pharisee's table Jesus teaches guests to take the lowest place and hosts to invite the poor. He tells of a great banquet whose invited guests refuse to come, and calls disciples to count the cost.

Luke 15

The Lost Sheep, Coin, and Son

Luke 15

Luke 15

The Lost Sheep, Coin, and Son

To grumbling Pharisees Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one, and a woman who searches for a lost coin. A father runs to embrace his returning prodigal son: 'He was lost and is found.'

Luke 16

The Rich Man and Lazarus

Luke 16

Luke 16

The Rich Man and Lazarus

Jesus tells of a shrewd manager and teaches that no one can serve both God and money. A rich man ignores the beggar Lazarus at his gate and finds the roles reversed beyond the grave.

Luke 17

Ten Healed of Leprosy

Luke 17

Luke 17

Ten Healed of Leprosy

Jesus heals ten lepers, and only one — a Samaritan — returns to give thanks. He teaches that the kingdom of God is in their midst and speaks of the day the Son of Man is revealed.

Luke 18

The Persistent Widow

Luke 18

Luke 18

The Persistent Widow

Jesus tells of a widow whose persistence wins justice, and of a tax collector whose humble prayer is heard over a Pharisee's. He welcomes little children, challenges a rich ruler, and gives sight to a blind beggar near Jericho.

Luke 19

Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

Luke 19

Luke 19

Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

Jesus calls Zacchaeus down from a sycamore tree, and salvation comes to his house. He enters Jerusalem to shouts of praise, weeps over the city, and clears the temple.

Luke 20

Questions of Authority

Luke 20

Luke 20

Questions of Authority

The leaders challenge Jesus' authority, and he answers with the parable of the wicked tenants. He turns their traps about Caesar's taxes and the resurrection back on them.

Luke 21

Signs of the End

Luke 21

Luke 21

Signs of the End

Jesus honors a poor widow's two small coins above all the rich gifts. He foretells the temple's destruction and the coming of the Son of Man, urging his followers to watch and pray.

Luke 22

The Last Supper

Luke 22

Luke 22

The Last Supper

Jesus shares the Passover with his apostles — 'This is my body, given for you' — while Judas agrees to betray him. He prays in anguish on the Mount of Olives, is arrested, and Peter denies him three times.

Luke 23

The Crucifixion

Luke 23

Luke 23

The Crucifixion

Pilate and Herod find no guilt in Jesus, yet the crowd demands his crucifixion. On the cross Jesus forgives his executioners, promises paradise to a dying criminal, and commits his spirit to the Father.

Luke 24

The Resurrection

Luke 24

Luke 24

The Resurrection

Women find the tomb empty, and two disciples recognize the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread at Emmaus. Jesus appears to the gathered disciples, opens the Scriptures, and is carried up into heaven.

his 1954 Genesis portion in Luyia was published by the British and Foreign Bible Society for the Luyia (Luhya) communities of western Kenya. Luyia (ISO 639-3 luy) is a Bantu macrolanguage of the Great Lakes group, covering more than a dozen mutually related varieties (Bukusu, Maragoli, Idakho, Isukha, Tiriki, Wanga, Tachoni, and others) spoken by some 6 million people across Kakamega, Bungoma, Vihiga, Busia, and Trans-Nzoia counties (Ethnologue: luy).

The Bible Societies in the colonial period worked from a "common Luyia" or Oluluhyia text, attempting to bridge the dialect divisions through a literary standard largely based on Wanga and Maragoli. A Luyia New Testament in this standard appeared in 1947, and Old Testament portions were issued through the 1950s and 1960s before a complete Luyia Bible reached publication.

The 1954 Genesis booklet sits in that interwar Old Testament programme. Subsequent decades brought separate translations into the major individual Luyia varieties (Bukusu Bible 2008, Lulogooli Bible 1975, Lwidakho New Testament 1976, Lutachoni portions, and Wanga revisions), gradually displacing the common-language standard in many congregations. The 1954 portion remains historically important as part of the only sustained common-Luyia scripture programme, distributed through Friends, Anglican, Mill Hill Catholic, and emerging Pentecostal congregations across the Western Province.

he 1975 Oluluyia Genesis is a Scripture portion in Luyia, a cluster of closely related Bantu varieties of the Great Lakes (Masaba-Luhya) group spoken by about 6.8 million Luyia people in western Kenya and adjoining districts of eastern Uganda (Ethnologue: luy, with distinct codes for the major varieties). The principal Luyia varieties include Bukusu, Logooli, Wanga, Marachi, Idakho-Isukha-Tiriki, Nyala, Saamia, Khayo, and several others.

Scripture work among the Luyia dates from the Church Missionary Society and Friends African Industrial Mission efforts in the 1900s and 1910s. Early portions appeared in individual varieties, including Logooli Mark in 1912 and a Wanga New Testament in the 1930s. The Bible Society of Kenya undertook the preparation of a Common Oluluyia (Luloogooli-Lwanga) Scripture edition from the 1960s, aimed at producing a register intelligible across the main Luyia varieties.

The 1975 Oluluyia Genesis is part of this common-language programme. It uses the Latin-script orthography standardised by the Luyia translation committee with marks for vowel length and for the voiced-implosive bilabial that distinguishes Luyia from neighbouring Luo and Kalenjin orthographies. Separate Scripture editions in Bukusu and Logooli continued in parallel. The common Luyia Bible was completed in later decades, with a Bukusu Bible appearing in 2005 and further variety-specific editions since.

items.title: Two Births Foretold
items.description: The angel Gabriel announces the coming births of John the Baptist to Zechariah and of Jesus to the virgin Mary. Mary sings praise to God, and John is born to Elizabeth in her old age.

items.title: The Birth of Jesus
items.description: Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger, and angels announce the news to shepherds. He is presented in the temple, and at twelve years old amazes the teachers in his Father's house.

items.title: The Ministry of John the Baptist
items.description: John preaches a baptism of repentance at the Jordan and points to one greater who is coming. Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends like a dove, and his family line is traced back to Adam.

items.title: Temptation and Rejection at Nazareth
items.description: Jesus fasts forty days in the wilderness and overcomes the devil's temptations with Scripture. In the Nazareth synagogue he announces that Isaiah's promise is fulfilled, and his own town drives him out.

items.title: Calling the First Disciples
items.description: After a miraculous catch of fish, Peter, James, and John leave their boats to follow Jesus. Jesus cleanses a leper, forgives and heals a paralyzed man, and calls Levi the tax collector.

items.title: Lord of the Sabbath
items.description: Jesus declares the Son of Man Lord of the Sabbath and chooses twelve apostles. On a level place he blesses the poor, commands love for enemies, and tells of two builders — one on rock, one on sand.

items.title: The Centurion's Faith
items.description: Jesus marvels at a Roman centurion's faith and raises a widow's only son at Nain. He answers John the Baptist's question from prison, and a sinful woman washes his feet with her tears.

items.title: The Parable of the Sower
items.description: Jesus tells the parable of the sower and calms a storm with a word. He frees a man possessed by a legion of demons, heals a bleeding woman, and raises Jairus's daughter.

items.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
items.description: Jesus sends out the Twelve, feeds five thousand, and Peter confesses him as God's Messiah. On the mountain Jesus is transfigured in glory, then sets his face toward Jerusalem.

items.title: The Good Samaritan
items.description: Jesus sends out seventy-two messengers ahead of him and rejoices in the Father's revelation to little children. He answers 'Who is my neighbor?' with the parable of the good Samaritan, and Mary chooses the better part at his feet.

items.title: Teaching on Prayer
items.description: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray, 'Father, hallowed be your name.' He casts out demons by the finger of God, and pronounces woes on Pharisees who clean the outside of the cup.

items.title: Do Not Be Afraid, Little Flock
items.description: Jesus warns against hypocrisy and greed, telling of a rich fool whose life ends the night his barns are full. He calls his followers to trust the Father who feeds the ravens, and to be ready for the Son of Man's coming.

items.title: The Narrow Door
items.description: Jesus calls all to repent, heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath, and likens the kingdom to a mustard seed. He urges entry through the narrow door and weeps over Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets.

items.title: The Great Banquet
items.description: At a Pharisee's table Jesus teaches guests to take the lowest place and hosts to invite the poor. He tells of a great banquet whose invited guests refuse to come, and calls disciples to count the cost.

items.title: The Lost Sheep, Coin, and Son
items.description: To grumbling Pharisees Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one, and a woman who searches for a lost coin. A father runs to embrace his returning prodigal son: 'He was lost and is found.'

items.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
items.description: Jesus tells of a shrewd manager and teaches that no one can serve both God and money. A rich man ignores the beggar Lazarus at his gate and finds the roles reversed beyond the grave.

items.title: Ten Healed of Leprosy
items.description: Jesus heals ten lepers, and only one — a Samaritan — returns to give thanks. He teaches that the kingdom of God is in their midst and speaks of the day the Son of Man is revealed.

items.title: The Persistent Widow
items.description: Jesus tells of a widow whose persistence wins justice, and of a tax collector whose humble prayer is heard over a Pharisee's. He welcomes little children, challenges a rich ruler, and gives sight to a blind beggar near Jericho.

items.title: Zacchaeus the Tax Collector
items.description: Jesus calls Zacchaeus down from a sycamore tree, and salvation comes to his house. He enters Jerusalem to shouts of praise, weeps over the city, and clears the temple.

items.title: Questions of Authority
items.description: The leaders challenge Jesus' authority, and he answers with the parable of the wicked tenants. He turns their traps about Caesar's taxes and the resurrection back on them.

items.title: Signs of the End
items.description: Jesus honors a poor widow's two small coins above all the rich gifts. He foretells the temple's destruction and the coming of the Son of Man, urging his followers to watch and pray.

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description: Jesus shares the Passover with his apostles — 'This is my body, given for you' — while Judas agrees to betray him. He prays in anguish on the Mount of Olives, is arrested, and Peter denies him three times.

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description: Pilate and Herod find no guilt in Jesus, yet the crowd demands his crucifixion. On the cross Jesus forgives his executioners, promises paradise to a dying criminal, and commits his spirit to the Father.

items.title: The Resurrection
items.description: Women find the tomb empty, and two disciples recognize the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread at Emmaus. Jesus appears to the gathered disciples, opens the Scriptures, and is carried up into heaven.

original.book_description: The Gospel of Luke offers the most comprehensive and orderly account of Jesus' life, written by a physician for a Greek audience. Luke emphasizes Jesus' compassion for the poor, outcasts, women, and sinners, showing how God's salvation extends to all people. Rich in parables and detailed narratives, Luke traces Jesus' journey from His birth in Bethlehem through His ministry in Galilee to His final days in Jerusalem.
